answer: Entry is priced by re-clearing, not by tickets. (1) Every epoch incumbents post sealed bids for shared compute; a nebula beacon randomises tie order. (2) A newcomer pays the externality it creates: the kernel re-clears the market without it, then bills the drift in each displaced bid, refunding those displaced. (3) k seats added together each displace the other k-1, so the bill sums near k squared units, while a lone agent owes one drift. (4) Splitting wallets changes nothing, because bids key on capacity, not on identity. A garden of puppets cannot bid as a single shadow.
